title: Election night surprise on financial sector stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. I'll estimate normal returns using the market model over the estimation window [-10,-2], then calculate abnormal returns (AR) and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window [0,+3]. The key assumption is that in the absence of the election surprise, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns as estimated during the pre-event period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s15_data.csv")

# Step 1: Estimate market model parameters for each stock using estimation window [-10, -2]
estimation_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2)

# Calculate market model parameters (alpha and beta) for each stock
market_model_params <- estimation_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    alpha = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[1],
    beta_estimated = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[2],
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Step 2: Calculate abnormal returns for event window [0, +3]
event_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 3) %>%
  left_join(market_model_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret = alpha + beta_estimated * mkt_ret,
    abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret
  )

# Step 3: Calculate daily average abnormal returns and CARs
daily_ar <- event_data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_ar = mean(abnormal_ret),
    se_ar = sd(abnormal_ret) / sqrt(n()),
    t_stat = avg_ar / se_ar,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("Daily Average Abnormal Returns:")
print(daily_ar)

# Step 4: Calculate CAR for [0,+3] window
car_data <- event_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    car_0_3 = sum(abnormal_ret),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Calculate average CAR and statistical significance
avg_car <- mean(car_data$car_0_3)
se_car <- sd(car_data$car_0_3) / sqrt(nrow(car_data))
t_stat_car <- avg_car / se_car
p_value_car <- 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat_car), df = nrow(car_data) - 1)

cat("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Average CAR[0,+3]: %.4f\n", avg_car))
cat(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f\n", se_car))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %.2f\n", t_stat_car))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", p_value_car))

# Step 5: Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# Check 1: CAR for [+1,+3] window (pure market reaction)
car_1_3 <- event_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_1_3 = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

avg_car_1_3 <- mean(car_1_3$car_1_3)
se_car_1_3 <- sd(car_1_3$car_1_3) / sqrt(nrow(car_1_3))
t_stat_1_3 <- avg_car_1_3 / se_car_1_3

cat(sprintf("CAR[+1,+3]: %.4f (t=%.2f)\n", avg_car_1_3, t_stat_1_3))

# Check 2: Test for pre-event drift (placebo test on [-3,-1])
placebo_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= -3 & event_day <= -1) %>%
  left_join(market_model_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret = alpha + beta_estimated * mkt_ret,
    abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret
  )

car_placebo <- placebo_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_placebo = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

avg_car_placebo <- mean(car_placebo$car_placebo)
se_car_placebo <- sd(car_placebo$car_placebo) / sqrt(nrow(car_placebo))
t_stat_placebo <- avg_car_placebo / se_car_placebo

cat(sprintf("Placebo CAR[-3,-1]: %.4f (t=%.2f)\n", avg_car_placebo, t_stat_placebo))

# Check 3: Cross-sectional variation by beta
high_beta <- car_data %>% 
  left_join(select(data, stock_id, beta) %>% distinct(), by = "stock_id") %>%
  filter(beta > median(beta))

low_beta <- car_data %>% 
  left_join(select(data, stock_id, beta) %>% distinct(), by = "stock_id") %>%
  filter(beta <= median(beta))

cat(sprintf("High-beta stocks CAR: %.4f\n", mean(high_beta$car_0_3)))
cat(sprintf("Low-beta stocks CAR: %.4f\n", mean(low_beta$car_0_3)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and statistically significant CAR in the [0,+3] window, likely in the range of 2-4%. Financial stocks typically benefit from unexpected election outcomes that signal deregulation or business-friendly policies. The effect should be stronger for high-beta financial stocks due to their greater sensitivity to systematic risk factors. The [+1,+3] window should show similar or stronger effects than [0,+3] since the election result was announced after market close on day 0.
